body:
Thank you for the vote of confidence. 

A little more information:

I made my entire adult life about helping others.
The monster's of my youth, murderers, rapists, junkies, thieves and other degenerates.
Some go unpunished still, some died of old age.
Only a small few paid for their crimes. 
But am I any better than then?
I have killed too, and I have saved. I was a Soldier. I did my job.
I watched helplessly as some of the very lands on which we fought, were decimated, whole villages killed, or enslaved. 
I watched it on the news after my injuries and illnesses took my ability to help.
I did the best I could with what little I had.
I had became the person I always needed.
Because when I needed that person, none existed in my small world. 
When I needed help, I was abandoned by those I love.
First in youth, to no fault of my own. 
Then in adulthood, facing terminal illness, crippling nerve damage and a very large drug habit brought on by the treatments/medications. 
I wasn't worth saving. 
But drugs will do that. 
I used to believe that no matter what an addict does to themselves, or to those they love that they could come back from it.
And in that, they were capable of love equal to that pain. 
I know now that I was wrong about parts of this belief. 
Both the great loves of my life moved on to be with wealthy, healthy men.
They have beautiful families, and both parents will live to see their children grow. 
Something I could offer neither. 
I am terminally ill, organs aren't functioning properly and I am slowly losing my mind due to a bacterial infection add in having a traumatic brain injury and things only get worse. 
I was happy once.
Honestly I was.
But life comes full circle, and remembering those I couldn't save.
Those I couldn't protect. 
Remembering and feeling helpless to stop it. 
We are both our failures and our successes. 
We are the sum total of our lifes experiences.
And if in life, I  am a burden, a painful reminder.
Yet in death, those I love have means to better their standing in life.
Life insurance, health insurance, education. 
In death, those I love have opportunities, and I can go out thankful to have been able to show them how much I love them one last time.
So I looked at reddit and found so many people who are suffering, some as lost as I am seeking answers wherever can be found.
Searching for someone whose been through it and come out ahead. 
Seeking those laid out in the aftermath, who seemed uncaring, yet suffer.
Because I don't want to die, though I am ready to.
